questions.topic: Default value of a String variable
questions.question: What is the default value of a String variable in Java if not initialized?
questions.solution: (a) null. A String is a reference type, so an uninitialised String instance variable holds null.

questions.question: What happens when you try to modify a String object in Java?

questions.solution: (b) A new String object is created. Strings are immutable, so methods like toUpperCase() or replace() return a new String and leave the original unchanged.

questions.solution: indexOf() returns the index of the first occurrence of a character (or substring) in a string, or -1 if it is not found. Return type: int.

marking_points.point: Purpose (first occurrence index, -1 if absent) and return type int

questions.topic: Purpose and return type of compareTo()
questions.question: State the purpose and return data type of the following String function: compareTo()
questions.solution: compareTo() compares two strings lexicographically (by character codes). It returns 0 if they are equal, a negative number if the calling string comes first, and a positive number if it comes after (the value is the difference of the first unequal characters, or of the lengths). Return type: int.

marking_points.point: Purpose (lexicographic comparison: 0 / negative / positive) and return type int

concepts: String is a class in java.lang
questions.question: Explain briefly how Java manages strings?
questions.solution: In Java a string is not a plain array of characters: it is an object of the String class (java.lang). String objects are immutable, so methods such as toUpperCase(), replace() or substring() return a new String instead of changing the original. String literals are stored in a string pool, so identical literals share one object, while new String(...) creates a separate object. The String class provides methods (length(), charAt(), indexOf(), compareTo(), equals(), etc.) to work with strings, and values of other types can be converted to and from strings (String.valueOf(), Integer.parseInt()).

marking_points.point: Strings are objects of the String class (not char arrays)
Immutability / new object on modification, with methods to manipulate strings
